## VIC block-tridiagonal assembly: the Roe-linearised flux divergence along a column (`vic_assemble_full_impl`) {#sec-ch07-vic-assembly}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** For every cell of a column, builds the three blocks $a_i$, $b_i$, $c_i$ of the implicit
system: the linearisation of the $x_1$ flux divergence, with Roe upwind dissipation frozen at the current state.
**Switch.** `integration/implicit-scheme` 1 (3 x 3) or 9 (5 x 5).
**Order.** A linearisation about the stage state.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch07-vic-blocks.
:::

The VIC replaces the explicit $x_1$ flux divergence by an implicit one. It does not re-solve the Riemann
problem. It linearises a Roe flux about the current state, holding the dissipation matrix $\lvert\hat A\rvert$ fixed, so the
correction is one linear block-tridiagonal solve per column. The gravity rows of the operator ($\Phi$ and the
face work) are part of @sec-ch06 and are not described here.

### Derivation

Write the Roe flux at face $i+\tfrac12$ as
$\hat F_{i+1/2} = \tfrac12(F_i + F_{i+1}) - \tfrac12\lvert\hat A\rvert_{i+1/2}(\mathbf q_{i+1}-\mathbf q_i)$, with
$\lvert\hat A\rvert = R\lvert\Lambda\rvert R^{-1}$ at the Roe average of the two cells. The update of cell $i$ with face areas $A_i$,
$A_{i+1}$ and volume $V_i$ is $\mathbf q_i/\Delta t + (A_{i+1}\hat F_{i+1/2} - A_i\hat F_{i-1/2})/V_i$.
Differentiating with $\lvert\hat A\rvert$ frozen and writing $J_i = \partial F/\partial\mathbf q$ at cell $i$ gives the three
blocks of row $i$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
a_i &= \frac{1}{2V_i}\Big(A_i\lvert\hat A\rvert_{i-1/2} + A_{i+1}\lvert\hat A\rvert_{i+1/2} + (A_{i+1}-A_i)J_i\Big) + \frac{I}{\Delta t}, \\
b_i &= -\frac{A_i}{2V_i}\big(\lvert\hat A\rvert_{i-1/2} + J_{i-1}\big), \\
c_i &= -\frac{A_{i+1}}{2V_i}\big(\lvert\hat A\rvert_{i+1/2} - J_{i+1}\big).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch07-vic-blocks}

The check builds these from the ported kernels on a spherical shell and compares them with central differences
of the frozen-$\lvert\hat A\rvert$ residual. They agree to $8\times10^{-9}$ of the block size [check
`src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_assembly_check.py`, output `vic_assembly_check.out`, `[C3]`]. Three properties carry
the construction:

1. The coded left eigenvectors invert the right ones (`[C1]`).
2. $R\Lambda R^{-1}$ with signed eigenvalues is the flux Jacobian at the Roe state, and it has the Roe property
   $\hat A(\mathbf q_R-\mathbf q_L) = F_R - F_L$ for one $\gamma$ (`[C2]`).
3. With no transverse velocity the 3 x 3 partial system is the full one restricted to $(\rho,\rho u,E)$. With
   transverse velocity the partial solve drops the coupling, by $3.7\times10^{-3}$ relative at 50 m/s in the
   check (`[C4]`).

In the code, @eq-ch07-vic-blocks is the block set-up with `half_inv_vol` $=1/(2V_i)$ ([`vic_assemble_full_impl.h:89-99`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h#L89-L99)).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch07-vic-stencil for the block row.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-vic-stencil
#| fig-cap: "The block row of cell $i$. The Roe dissipation matrices $\\lvert\\hat A\\rvert$ sit on the two faces (orange) with the face areas $A_i$, $A_{i+1}$; the flux Jacobians $J$ sit in the three cells (blue). The coefficients $a_i$, $b_i$, $c_i$ combine them as in @eq-ch07-vic-blocks. The gravity block $\\Phi$ belongs to the gravity chapter."
#| fig-alt: "Three cells in a row with orange faces between them, labelled with the Roe matrices and face areas, and the formulas for b, c and a underneath."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.fig_vic_stencil import make_fig
make_fig()
```

Each face takes its two neighbours' primitives. `RoeAverage` weights by $\sqrt\rho$ and averages the total
enthalpy ([`flux_decomposition_impl.h:37-68`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/flux_decomposition_impl.h#L37-L68)); the caller passes the mean $\gamma$ of the two cells.
`Eigenvalue` returns $|u-c|$, $|u|$, $|u+c|$, $|u|$, $|u|$ ([`flux_decomposition_impl.h:70-74`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/flux_decomposition_impl.h#L70-L74)).
`Eigenvector` writes out the eigenvectors and their inverse by hand
([`flux_decomposition_impl.h:76-103`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/flux_decomposition_impl.h#L76-L103)), and `FluxJacobian` the Euler flux Jacobian in conserved
variables ([`flux_decomposition_impl.h:105-126`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/flux_decomposition_impl.h#L105-L126)). The full kernel forms $\lvert\hat A\rvert$ as `Am` and `Ap`
at the lower and upper face ([`vic_assemble_full_impl.h:51-87`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h#L51-L87)) and then the blocks, with `half_inv_vol` $=1/(2V_i)$ ([`vic_assemble_full_impl.h:89-99`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h#L89-L99)). The partial kernel copies
the $(\rho, \rho u, E)$ rows and columns out of the same 5 x 5 matrices into `Am2` and `Ap2`
([`vic_assemble_partial_impl.h:110-120`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/vic_assemble_partial_impl.h#L110-L120)).

On the CPU the assembly runs the columns in parallel and fills each cell independently. A solid cell gets
$a=I/\Delta t$, $b=c=0$, and its fluid neighbour sees a mirror of itself instead of the solid's state; both are
in `vic_assemble_full_cpu` ([`implicit_dispatch.cpp:77-131`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cpp#L77-L131)), as the check confirms (`[C5]`). Before the assembly, the host
removes the EOS reference energy from the energy tendency and takes $\gamma$ from the EOS, through
`internal_energy_offset` ([`hydro/hydro.cpp:427-435`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L427-L435)). It also rotates the velocity into the local orthonormal frame, through
`prim2local1_` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:226-231`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L226-L231)).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The operator is a linearisation with $\lvert\hat A\rvert$ frozen. It is not the Jacobian of the explicit Riemann solver
the stage used, so the implicit and explicit fluxes are not the same function.
:::

1. **Mean $\gamma$.** The Roe average at a face uses the mean $\gamma$ of the two cells. The Roe property holds
   only when they are equal (`[C2]` tests one $\gamma$).
2. **Partial system.** `vic-partial` ignores the transverse momentum coupling, which is exact only when $v=w=0$
   (`[C4]`).
3. **No direct test of the blocks.** No ctest compares $a$, $b$, $c$ with a difference quotient. The column tests
   check rest states only.
